summary.problem: Executing /stats session after resuming a session displays a newly generated session ID rather than the resumed session's ID.
summary.root_cause: useSessionResume.ts does not call uiTelemetryService.hydrate() with the resumed conversation data when resuming a session. As a result, uiTelemetryService does not emit a clear/update event with the resumed session ID, causing SessionStatsProvider to retain its initial startup session ID.
summary.context: Session statistics in the CLI are managed by SessionStatsProvider in SessionContext.tsx, which subscribes to events from uiTelemetryService. While in-session browser resumption in useSessionBrowser.ts properly hydrates telemetry via uiTelemetryService.hydrate(), command-line session resumption handled by useSessionResume.ts was missing this call.

steps: In loadHistoryForResume inside useSessionResume.ts, call uiTelemetryService.hydrate(resumedData.conversation) when restoring the session history.
In packages/cli/src/ui/contexts/SessionContext.tsx, update SessionStatsProvider's effect to update stats.sessionId whenever the sessionId prop changes.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When a session is resumed via useSessionResume, uiTelemetryService.hydrate() is called with the resumed conversation record, updating telemetry state and ensuring /stats session displays the correct resumed session ID.
verification_steps: Add a test in packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useSessionResume.test.ts verifying that uiTelemetryService.hydrate is called with resumedData.conversation during loadHistoryForResume.
Run unit tests for useSessionResume via vitest to confirm all tests pass.

github_metadata.title: Wrong session id shown after resuming a session
